_meta.schema: pattern: id, match (literal substring, matched case-insensitively against the assembled command AND against its unquoted projection), label, why, blast_floor — UI spec v1 §4 (red confirmation banner) and §8 (maintainable data table, not scattered string checks)
_meta.status: CR-T-02 skeleton — the destructive patterns the UI spec names by example. The banner that consumes this table lands with the command assembler (CR-T-15).
_meta.rule: This table is data so a content reviewer can extend it without touching the renderer. A command matching any row forces the red confirmation banner and holds Copy until the reviewer checkbox is set. A pattern may span a value: the assembler quotes every value, so `rm -rf /` is matched against the unquoted projection `rm -rf /etc/pki` as well as against the raw `rm -rf '/etc/pki'` (MCR-SEC-008). Every row in this table is asserted to fire on a synthetic assembled command by tests/hostile_harness.js — a pattern that can never match fails the build.

patterns.label: Recursive force delete
patterns.why: Removes a directory tree with no prompt and no recovery on a local filesystem.

patterns.label: Recursive force delete from an absolute path
patterns.why: Recursive deletion rooted at an absolute path: on / or a mount point this is unrecoverable, and the target is the value the operator just typed.

patterns.label: Filesystem signature wipe
patterns.why: Erases filesystem, RAID, and partition-table signatures from a block device.

patterns.label: Logical volume removal
patterns.why: Destroys a logical volume and every filesystem on it.

patterns.label: Volume group removal
patterns.why: Destroys a volume group and the logical volumes inside it.

patterns.label: Filesystem creation over a device
patterns.why: Formats a block device, discarding whatever it held.

patterns.label: Account deletion
patterns.why: Removes an account, and with -r its home directory and mail spool.

patterns.label: Package removal
patterns.why: Package removal pulls dependent packages with it; on a running host that can take a service down.

patterns.label: Service stop and disable
patterns.why: Stops the unit immediately and prevents it starting at boot.

patterns.label: Package removal (yum)
patterns.why: Package removal pulls dependent packages with it; on a running host that can take a service down. RHEL 7 uses yum, not dnf.
